newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians, Israelis clash in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians, Israelis clash in Hebron.

text.p: Hundreds of Palestinians stoned Israeli soldiers in the narrow market alleys of Hebron on Friday during protests against the building of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Troops in full battle gear fired rubber bullets and teargas, lightly injuring up to four youths, witnesses said.
It was the worst unrest in Hebron since Israel handed 80 percent of the West Bank city over to President Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority in January.
Demonstrators also hurled several firebombs, damaging an army jeep, witnesses said.
Jewish settlers, who are guarded by the army in the Israeli-controlled heart of Hebron, threw stones back at the Palestinians.
Soldiers charged demonstrators and briefly detained three. But the troops freed them when they came under a heavy barrage of stones.
Israel Radio said that Arafat's West Bank security chief, Jibril Rajoub, was on his way to Hebron.
Israeli security forces are on alert for protests in the West Bank and East Jerusalem after Moslem prayers at noon on Friday. Palestinians planned marches in several towns.
Tension has been high since Israel's right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sent bulldozers last Tuesday to a hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem to begin a Jewish settlement.
Arafat has urged Palestinians to shun violent protests. He ordered his nearly 30,000-strong police force to prevent clashes.
Palestinian police evacuated demonstrators who were overcome by teargas. Some officers signalled to the Israelis to stop firing gas and bullets but the clashes continued.
Up to five soldiers were hit by stones, witnesses said.
Last September 61 Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers were killed in gunbattles after Netanyahu opened a tunnel entrance near Moslem holy places in Jerusalem.
